title: Four patterns that actually use Jev

items.name: Speculative fan-out
items.what: Send every question the code might need, including ones that only matter on some paths.
items.why: Questions run in parallel. Unused answers are cheap. Serial calls re-pay the state.

items.name: Confidence-gated routing
items.what: Treat confidence as a second axis: act / confirm / human.
items.why: A peaked distribution is a different signal from the winning label.
items.code_owns: Thresholds, and the fact that irreversible actions need a higher bar.

items.name: Composite scoring
items.what: Split a fuzzy judgment into atomic scores, then weight them in code.
items.why: When the team disagrees with the combined result, you change weights — not a prompt.
items.code_owns: Weights, caps, and the final formula.

items.name: Intent routing
items.what: Classify the request, then dispatch to deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a person.
items.why: Jev is fast enough to sit on the hot path in front of expensive generation.
items.code_owns: The handler map and what happens on low confidence.
